Was this a winner or a loser?

author: Jurij
text:
In the dissection room we talked about targets and origins.

The big question was whether price, after an eng, wants the origin, intended as the first engulf in a move up/down (extreme origin) or just the next obvious FL?

Many times IF wrote on his charts after an eng "FTR - easy traget" looking like the sure target is always the first engulf up/down after trend change.

This works only if there's nothing in the way (important level) before the origin.

omidfxt wrote: Hey Jurij

I hadn't enough details on your charts but here is what i think about it:

Yes as you wrote it was a good target because it trapped traders (FL below a low) and was holding price up later.

But I think there was more to it tomake it such an important FL.

corsica wrote: I agree with Omid,

It looks like the "tg hit ?" level sits between 2 ftrs hence the tg wasn't hit and the ftr in the blue box seems to be the level to aim for.

Really interesting , thank you Jurij !

As you see I took this trade and I lost, but learned a valuable lesson.

I had the same thought as you, that the levels sits between 2 FTRs and that price should be able to make it to the origin.

But the FL was also important because it was aligned with a swap zone (SR flip or just symmetry):

I think without this past SR structure price would have gone to the origin.

So my little aha moment was that the assumption that price just wants the extreme origin is too simple and not always true (if there's a swap level). I think we must always look for symmetry and swap zones to make sure to not miss an important target.

I remember now in the
 first webinar
 IF explains what the origin is, he says that once an important level is broken (such as SR/RS) a new origin of the move is created (FL).

Here some charts:

My understanding is constantly evolving, what is true for me today could be wrong tomorrow, so please if you know better and think this is wrong, please let me know

Any comments are always welcome
